title: CoherentFormalModulesCoimageImage
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf. Equip $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] with any structures providing a kernel and a cokernel for each arrow. For every arrow $\alpha:F\to G$, the canonical comparison $\operatorname{Coker}(\ker(\alpha)\to F)\to\operatorname{Ker}(G\to\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha))$ is an isomorphism. Kernels and cokernels here are taken inside $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, not termwise.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), last paragraph of the proof of part (1), Coim=Im

proof.text: Use the kernel construction of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module-kernel] and termwise cokernels supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-cokernel-closure]. Restriction to an affine open preserves these constructions: images, kernels and ideal products restrict, quotient maps restrict by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and any enlarged stabilization constant gives the same eventual quotient system. The restricted kernel is thus the system with affine sections $K/I^nK$, where $K=\ker f$ in the affine equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine]. Noetherianity of the completion [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] ensures that $K$ is finite. The equivalence similarly identifies the cokernel with $\operatorname{Coker}f$.

The additive affine equivalence sends the canonical comparison to $M/\ker f\to\operatorname{im} f$ induced by $f$. The first isomorphism theorem for modules makes this invertible, and an equivalence reflects isomorphisms. Consequently every component is locally invertible. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-isomorphism-local] to the affine cover to obtain invertibility globally.

Arbitrary choices of kernels and cokernels are uniquely isomorphic to the constructions above by their universal properties. These isomorphisms conjugate the canonical comparison, which remains invertible. In particular the statement holds for the arbitrary structures in its Lean hypotheses.
